category_title: Silent and depressed EMLLs experiencing extreme language-related frustration and school avoidance
minimal_context: Jessica is participating in whole-class instruction where she is asked to read yellow signs placed on a classroom bookcase.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jessica, please look at the yellow signs on the bookcase and tell the class what they say.

STUDENT: No.

TUTOR: Why don't you give it a try?

STUDENT: (Makes a weak smile and shakes her head quietly.)

TUTOR: Do you understand what we are doing right now?

STUDENT: (Shows a depressed and helpless look) 어.그게.사실 선생님이 뭐라고 하는지 하나도 모르겠어요. Umm…honestly…I have no idea what she’s talking about.

options.A: Use opportunities to respond to maintain Jessica's orientation and engagement during the instruction.
options.B: Explicitly incorporate instructional elements that promote self-compassion for Jessica during the instruction.
options.C: Ask Jessica in Korean, whispering to check how well she understands the teacher.
options.D: Provide external regulation to help Jessica start inhibiting inappropriate urges during the instruction.
